Mina — quick read and a couple of datapoints from infra:

- Baseline pool (west1) has ~120 available slots that can be converted to Dedicated in ~7–10 days if we reserve additional NVLink nets; converting more quickly requires a manual procurement lead.
- The 4.0 SKU assumption looks right for the conv rates you're using; however latency-sensitive deals (Acme) will need isolated pools and that adds ~12% overhead to GPU requirement estimates.

If we want to avoid upgrades to networking, I can provide a soft-fallback plan that stages customers onto burst-first, then flips to Dedicated at the month boundary. That reduces up-front reserve pressure but increases short-term cost by ~18% for the July cohort.

Ben

ben_carter@redwood.com

Mina / all — I ran three scenarios against the backlog in the sheet:

1) Conservative reserve (50% of weighted forecast): add 60 Dedicated GPUs across west1 & east1; picks up the highest-confidence closes only.
2) Balanced reserve (80%): add 110 GPUs; requires moving two burst clusters into Dedicated with a 10-day lead.
3) Aggressive reserve (100%): add 140 GPUs; needs approval for expedited procurement and Opex buffer in July.

If finance is willing to accept the temporary opex impact, Balanced is the recommended tradeoff — minimizes churn while allowing two critical accounts (NIM, Acme) to test on Dedicated without degrading performance.

I'll attach the scenario CSV to the drive.

— Karthik
